description: Bias-control and editorial independence rules for PBJ320 public metadata. Investigative journalism may inform data architecture; it must not set product conclusions, labels, or operator-specific logic.
core_principle: PBJ320 should learn from public data joins and source-transparency patterns, not inherit advocacy, litigation strategy, or market-position framing from any single publisher or short seller.

evidence_tiers.observed_data: Independently collected or regulator-observed records (e.g., survey deficiencies, penalties tied to inspections).
evidence_tiers.payroll_submitted: Facility payroll records submitted to CMS through PBJ; auditable but not independently observed at the bedside.
evidence_tiers.facility_reported: Facility-submitted assessments or CMS calculations that rely on them (e.g., MDS-derived quality measures, case-mix).
evidence_tiers.pbj320_derived: Screening statistics, rankings, and comparisons computed by PBJ320 from public datasets.
evidence_tiers.third_party_allegation: Claims from lawsuits, interviews, or news reports not verified by PBJ320.
evidence_tiers.legal_conclusion: Determinations of violation, negligence, causation, or liability. PBJ320 public pages do not make these.

implementation_rules: Do not hard-code conclusions from any single investigative publisher into PBJ320 labels or methodology.
Do not create operator- or chain-specific public logic unless driven by user-supplied identifiers (e.g., CCN, entity id) with neutral copy.
Do not add anti-chain, anti-operator, pro-plaintiff, investor, or law-firm-oriented assumptions to public metadata.
Do not copy sensational labels (e.g., fatal neglect, fraud, gaming, care never delivered, profit from understaffing, tunneling).
Every new public metric must be defined from documented public data and PBJ320 method notes.
Every derived metric must carry a caveat distinguishing observed data, facility-reported data, verified findings, PBJ320 estimates, third-party allegations, and legal conclusions.
Benchmarks and thresholds must name a documented source; disable or omit when the formula or authority is not in the repo.
Future cost-report fields must use neutral labels such as related-party payments, not extraction, tunneling, or hidden profit.
Ownership and acquisition views must stay descriptive unless a causal model is fully documented and tested elsewhere.

related_party_payments.approved_caveat: Payments reported on Medicare cost reports between related parties. PBJ320 describes reported amounts; it does not classify intent or legality.

ownership_acquisition_staffing.approved_caveat: Descriptive comparison of reported PBJ staffing before and after a CMS change-of-ownership date. Not a causal estimate of ownership effects.

acuity_staffing_comparison.approved_caveat: Comparison to a documented acuity or case-mix benchmark from public CMS data. Not a dollarized gap, legal minimum, or proof of care not delivered.
